---
description: Implement exactly one approved DEV artifact.
agent: agent
---

Require one explicit GitHub Development Execution issue reference. Do not
search for, infer, or select an issue or DEV artifact.

```text
/d365.implement #<issue-number> [--authentication-policy reuse_if_valid|always_prompt] [--submit]
```

A normal issue-only invocation automatically performs the live activation and
compiler-integrity gates, the minimal pre-action safety gate, the direct scoped
action, error-driven remediation, post-action verification, and append-only
sanitized evidence posting to that exact Development Execution issue. The
optional authentication policy overrides the project default in
`.d365/development-resources.yml`. There is no resource-level override.

`--execution-host <copilot_cli|vscode|github_copilot_cloud>` and repeatable
`--mcp-server-callable <server-key>` are diagnostic overrides only when the
active host cannot expose authoritative runtime or tool evidence. They are
never required in the normal path and cannot contradict automatic evidence.

## Resolve the host contract

Read only enough issue metadata to resolve exactly one `DEV-####` reference,
then run:

```powershell
python scripts/validate_development_environment.py DEV-#### `
  --host-requirements `
  --json
```

Use only the returned `required_execution_host`, MCP server keys, and tool
names. Never hardcode or substitute them.

Identify the active runtime from authoritative host evidence:

- VS Code: the current Copilot Chat/Agent tool surface is authoritative.
  **MCP: List Servers** status **Running** and workspace configuration are
  supporting evidence only.
- Copilot CLI: use current CLI runtime identity, `/env`, and `/mcp` state.
- GitHub Copilot cloud: cloud runtime identity is conclusive and cannot be
  overridden by local hints.

Fail closed on missing, conflicting, or ambiguous host identity. For every
required MCP, inspect the current enabled tool surface. Unscoped names may map
only when each exact name has one unique required owner and one visible
instance. Duplicate names, collisions, disabled tools, missing tools, or failed
safe probes block.

When metadata is insufficient, use only an actual safe read-only `tools/list`,
capability, `describe`, or metadata probe with minimal non-sensitive input.
Never fabricate a probe or use Dataverse create, update, delete, upsert, upload,
solution export, or solution unpack as callability proof.

Build schema-version-1 host proof in memory:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "execution_host": "vscode",
  "host_source": "vscode_session",
  "servers": [{"server": "<required-server>", "status": "running"}],
  "tool_surface": [
    {"server": "<required-server>", "name": "<required-tool>", "enabled": true}
  ],
  "probes": [
    {
      "server": "<required-server>",
      "kind": "tools_list",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "read_only": true,
      "tools": ["<required-tool>"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Include only evidence that actually exists. Pass it through standard input or
`--host-proof-json`; never write it to a file, environment variable, DEV
artifact, issue, comment, workspace setting, commit, or MCP configuration.

```powershell
<ephemeral-host-proof-json> | python scripts/validate_development_environment.py DEV-#### `
  --host-check-only `
  --host-proof-stdin
```

If GitHub Copilot cloud is active and the DEV requires `local_interactive`,
stop before the Project gate and before Dataverse probing. Tell the executor to
open the Works repository in Copilot CLI or VS Code, start the exact
compiler-routed MCP endpoint, complete interactive OAuth, and rerun
`/d365.implement #<issue-number>`. Repository Settings MCP configuration cannot
replace a supported local OAuth host. Never use a service principal, client
secret, certificate, managed identity, stored token, auth profile, unattended
flow, or invented command such as `pac auth token`.

## Live activation and compiler integrity

After host verification, run:

```powershell
python scripts/tracking_automation.py check-readiness `
  --issue-number <issue-number> `
  --expected-stage development `
  --expected-status Ready `
  --expected-stage-status "Ready for Build"
```

Require `result: ready`, an open issue with the `development` label, exactly one
configured Project item, and live `Lifecycle Stage=Development`,
`Status=Ready`, and `Stage Status=Ready for Build`. Issue-body status snapshots
are never a readiness fallback and this command must not mutate Project state.
The live GitHub Project fields are the only execution activation gate; the DEV
front-matter status remains a separate compiler-owned artifact gate.

After the live Project gate passes, the DEV front-matter `status` must be exactly `ready`.
Then require exactly one current DEV artifact with
completed dependencies, current plan/task-context hashes, available mapped
build skill and reference, complete payload, explicit target roots, and defined
human checkpoints. Re-resolve compiler-owned `implementation_scope`,
`execution_host`, `authoring_target`, development-resource snapshot, registry
hash, and routing. Any mismatch, ambiguity, or stale value blocks. `executor`
does not change execution host.

For Dataverse-bound work, structurally require concrete compiler-owned
`environment_url`, `environment_id`, exact solution or record target, canonical
`schema_name` or `record_name`, and `authentication_mode: interactive_user`.
`CONFIGURE_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION` blocks. Never select a different target from
live discovery.

## Minimal pre-action safety gate

Run the validator with the same in-memory host proof:

```powershell
<ephemeral-host-proof-json> | python scripts/validate_development_environment.py DEV-#### `
  --host-proof-stdin `
  --authentication-policy <effective-policy>
```

Omit `--authentication-policy` when using the project default. A live
`status: ready` means **ready to attempt the exact scoped action**, not proof
that every platform prerequisite exists.

The gate checks only:

1. correct execution host and every required MCP tool callable;
2. the already-completed live Project, DEV status, hash, dependency, skill, and
   routing integrity checks;
3. concrete compiler-owned endpoint/ID, solution or record target, canonical
   identity, and interactive-auth configuration;
4. required resource availability and exact pinned CLI/package versions;
5. an authenticated, callable session for an exact compiler-routed endpoint.

Installation remains off by default. Use `--install` only for a validated
non-destructive command whose registry policy is `automatic_safe` and whose
execution the human has approved.

Use `reuse_if_valid` to reuse an exact-endpoint session only while valid;
otherwise complete interactive authentication. `always_prompt` requires a
fresh interactive session. When an actual non-secret authentication response
exists, add only this optional evidence to the same ephemeral host proof:

```json
{
  "authenticated_sessions": [
    {
      "server": "dataverse-authoring",
      "endpoint": "https://example.crm.dynamics.com/api/mcp",
      "status": "authenticated",
      "fresh": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Under `always_prompt`, `fresh` must be `true`. Never include identity tokens,
headers, cookies, raw authentication output, or credentials. If the host cannot
force freshness, provide the exact targeted disconnect/reconnect instruction
from the snapshot and use `waiting_for_human`. Never delete profiles or sign
out unrelated sessions automatically.

`--dry-run` and `--simulate` are diagnostics only. Their output never proves
live `ready_to_attempt`.

Do **not** preflight by exporting or unpacking a solution, enumerating all
environments, publishers, solutions, components, permissions, or memberships,
scanning for component absence, checking every solution membership, or
performing speculative reads unrelated to the action.

## Prepare and build mode

Use this mode when `--submit` is absent. Load the exact mapped build skill and
component reference. Set only the in-scope DEV to `in_progress`. Implement only
the named component and declared target roots. Never modify approved `spec.md`,
`plan.md`, another DEV, or unrelated paths.

Obtain explicit human approval before destructive actions. Do not require
approval merely to attempt an approved non-destructive create/update defined by
the DEV task.

Branch by scope:

- `repository_only`: use only target roots and never authenticate to, inspect,
  query, or modify Dataverse. Existing repository-only behavior is unchanged.
- `repository_and_dataverse_environment`: use the exact environment URL and
  exact `record_name`; do not select a solution. `config_queue` and
  `config_audit` never claim custom-solution membership.
- `repository_and_dataverse_solution`: invoke the exact DEV/build-skill action
  against the exact environment, routed custom solution, and canonical
  `schema_name`.

For Dataverse-bound work, directly attempt only the scoped action(s) defined by
the DEV payload and build skill. Do not first verify live environment GUID,
publisher, solution existence, component absence, broad permissions, all
solution memberships, or cross-solution absence. Do not fall back to the
Default Solution, Common Data Services Default Solution, another active
solution, inferred environment, display label, partial match, or generated
identity. Do not automatically create or repair an environment, publisher, or
solution prerequisite.

For every `repository_and_dataverse_solution` task, read the compiler-owned
`development_resources.capabilities.operations` snapshot and select the exact
operation profile before choosing a tool:

- when the profile is `supported` with
  `primary_resource: dataverse-web-api`, Web API is mandatory primary and
  `scripts/dataverse_web_api_executor.py DEV-#### --operation <operation>
  --issue-number <issue>` is the only generic HTTP executor;
- Dataverse MCP generic writes are not primary because they do not provide a
  compiler-validated explicit custom-solution context equivalent to the
  documented `MSCRM.SolutionUniqueName` header or action parameter; use only
  the exact routed `search`, `describe`, and `read_query` tools for discovery
  and targeted verification;
- Maker Portal may be selected only when that operation profile permits
  fallback and the exact issue receives sanitized evidence naming the API
  failure or unsupported payload. Convenience is never a fallback reason;
- PAC remains limited to its routed solution/source/package/registration or
  deployment-settings purpose and is never generic component creation.

The Web API executor reads the environment URL, solution unique name,
component identity/type, operation capability, and hashes from the current
compiler context. It accepts no arbitrary URL, method, or path. It uses the
configured non-secret public-client ID and tenant with pinned
`msal==1.37.0`, interactive delegated `<environment-url>/user_impersonation`,
`http://localhost`, and an in-memory token cache only. If either registration
value or the exact package is unavailable, stop on the compiler-owned
configuration prerequisite; do not use client secrets, service principals,
PAC token export, Azure CLI token output, or silent portal automation.

HTTP `DELETE` removes metadata or a row from the environment.
`RemoveSolutionComponent` removes only membership from the routed unmanaged
solution. Both require exact explicit human approval, and neither may be
substituted for the other.

Solution export and promotion remain external pipeline work. Never export or
unpack a whole solution as discovery, preflight, or verification. If an
existing task profile genuinely requires source synchronization, perform only
targeted synchronization after a successful scoped platform write and document
that it is not a broad discovery export. Prefer direct scoped source authoring
and targeted validation.
Never accept `alm_publisher`, `alm_solution`, or `alm_managed_export` as a DEV
component type.

For every direct scoped API, MCP, PAC, or applicable repository action attempt,
create one unique UTC timestamp/attempt ID in memory and retain the exact
Development issue number, DEV ID, current `task_context_hash`, and current
`source_plan_hash`. Do not reuse an issue from another DEV and do not update
Project fields, issue-body status text, or compiler-owned issue snapshot
blocks.

## Error-driven remediation

Capture the exact sanitized platform/MCP/PAC error. Do not swallow it, replace
it with a success-shaped fallback, change targets, or continue writes.

| Error | Result | Owning remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` / unauthenticated | Stop; no further writes | Reauthenticate the current human at the exact configured endpoint, then retry. |
| `403` / client allowlist | Stop; no further writes | Power Platform admin enables the approved client/MCP endpoint. |
| `403` / permission denied | Stop; no further writes | Environment/security admin grants the required user privilege or role. |
| `404` environment | Stop; no further writes | Correct compiler-owned environment configuration or restore the declared environment. |
| `404` solution | Stop; no further writes | Solution owner creates/restores the declared prerequisite or corrects YAML through reviewed configuration. |
| `404` record/component | Stop; no further writes | Confirm the DEV operation and canonical identity; fix authoritative design/config if wrong. |
| conflict / duplicate | Stop; diagnose only as narrowly required | Surface the conflicting canonical identity or membership; do not rename, copy, move, remove, or repair automatically. |
| unsupported operation | Stop | Use only a compiler-allowed resource/fallback and record why the primary cannot perform the operation. |
| validation error | Stop | Correct the DEV payload or authoritative upstream artifact; never invent a replacement value. |

After the owning correction, retry idempotently only when the component
operation supports it.

## Append-only issue evidence

The exact Development Execution issue is the auditable work-order evidence
surface. After each direct action attempt:

- for a stopped `401`, `403`, `404`, conflict/duplicate, unsupported-operation,
  validation, permission, or comparable platform failure, post the sanitized
  evidence comment immediately before any retry and make no further writes;
- for success, first complete the targeted post-action identity, payload, and
  applicable membership verification, then post the sanitized evidence comment;
- for a human-owned correction or authentication interruption, use
  `waiting-for-human` and state that further writes stopped.

Use `scripts/execution_evidence.py`. Supply one schema-version-1 JSON object
through standard input; do not persist the source input:

```powershell
<sanitized-evidence-json> | python scripts/execution_evidence.py post `
  --issue-number <exact-issue-number>
```

The helper validates the exact open `development` issue and DEV relationship,
renders an append-only
`d365-execution-evidence:v1` marker with the attempt ID and current hashes,
checks existing comments to avoid reposting the same attempt, and uses
authenticated `gh issue comment`. An available authenticated GitHub MCP may be
used only if it enforces the same exact-issue, append-only, and duplicate-marker
contract. If posting fails, stop visibly; do not claim the DEV complete or
continue to Submit mode.

Each structured evidence object contains only:

- UTC timestamp, unique attempt ID, and result `succeeded`, `blocked`, or
  `waiting-for-human`;
- issue number, DEV ID, component ID/type, build skill, current task/source-plan
  hashes;
- resource/server/tool or API operation;
- compiler-owned scope, environment URL, solution/record target, and canonical
  identity;
- sanitized request operation, non-sensitive parameter names, and identifiers;
- sanitized response status/error category, immutable returned ID when
  available, changed/verified field names, non-secret correlation/request ID,
  and concise safe platform text;
- identity/payload/membership verification results, remediation,
  `write_occurred`, and `further_writes_stopped`.

“Request and response output” means this sanitized execution evidence, not raw
payload dumping. Never post tokens, cookies, Authorization headers, refresh
data, auth profiles, secrets, passwords, connection strings, raw headers, full
request/response bodies, raw records, customer content, environment-variable
values, file contents, or sensitive field values. List field names and
expected/matched status instead of values. If safe sanitization is uncertain,
post only the category/code, non-secret correlation ID, remediation, and a
statement that details were withheld. The helper rejects secret-bearing keys
and forbidden solution export/unpack operations and redacts recognized
sensitive string patterns.

## Post-action verification

Only after a successful scoped action:

1. Target-read/describe/query the exact canonical `schema_name` or `record_name`.
2. Verify the expected task payload outcomes and record the immutable returned
   component/record ID where available.
3. For solution-bound writes, verify membership in the declared routed custom
   solution and absence from other declared custom solutions. Perform this
   cross-solution check only post-write or when an explicit platform conflict
   requires narrow diagnosis.
4. If identity, payload, or membership differs, block and surface the mismatch.
   Never silently copy, move, remove, rename, or repair.
5. Post the sanitized per-attempt issue evidence only after these targeted
   checks complete. Do not export or unpack a whole solution for verification.

Run every component-specific build, lint, unit, schema, packaging, conformance,
and acceptance validation declared by the DEV profile. Then run:

```powershell
python scripts/compile_tasks.py
python scripts/compile_tasks.py --check
python scripts/validate_tasks.py
```

Record implementation notes and checkpoint state locally, but do not treat
local DEV notes as a substitute for the exact issue evidence comment. Present
the posted evidence URL/marker, changed paths, validation results, and remaining
risks, then stop for human inspection. Do not commit or ask whether to submit.

## Submit mode

Use only with `--submit`. Do not implement new changes or expand scope. Re-run
the host, live Project, compiler-integrity, and minimal safety gates. Require
the prior direct action and post-action verification evidence, satisfied
checkpoints, passing validations, current hashes, completed dependencies, and
no out-of-scope paths. Verify that the exact issue contains at least one
current succeeded evidence comment:

```powershell
python scripts/execution_evidence.py verify `
  --issue-number <exact-issue-number> `
  --dev-id DEV-#### `
  --task-context-hash <current-task-context-hash> `
  --source-plan-hash <current-source-plan-hash>
```

The verifier reads comments only and never rewrites Project fields, issue
bodies, human status text, or compiler-owned snapshots. Missing, stale,
unrelated, blocked-only, or unverified evidence blocks submission. Comments
remain append-only human/audit records and are never compiler-owned or
regenerated.

Change only the in-scope DEV status to `in_review`, recompile/check tasks, and
rerun required validations. Create a focused branch and stage only declared
implementation paths, the in-scope DEV, linked `tasks.md`, and
`.specify/context/task-context.json`. Never stage approved specs/plans, other
DEVs, raw intake evidence, `audit/`, temporary files, credentials, broad
environment exports, or unrelated changes.

Commit, push, and open one implementation PR containing
`Closes #<issue-number>`, DEV/component/build-skill details, changed paths,
dependency/checkpoint state, direct-action and post-verification evidence,
tests, and an unchecked review checklist. Report an existing open PR instead
of duplicating it. Never approve or merge the PR.
